new_statements.translation: In this manuscript we do not include a section devoted to the prosody of Malalí. We limit ourselves to speculating that stress was not contrastive and fell on the last syllable of the (phonological?) word, given that this is the case in the best-known languages of the Trans-São-Franciscan family for which we have recordings and/or transcriptions made by trained linguists (Maxakalí, Ritual Maxakalí, Pataxó-Hãhãhãe and Krenák). Added to this is the fact that most of the diacritic accents present in the Malalí records are found on the last vowel of the word.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress presumed non-contrastive and word-final (last syllable of the phonological word), inferred from (a) uniform final stress in the documented sister languages Maxakalí, Ritual Maxakalí, Pataxó-Hãhãhãe and Krenák and (b) the placement of the sparse acute accents in Wied-Neuwied's (1815-17) and Saint-Hilaire's (c. 1817) wordlists, which fall mostly on the final vowel (e.g. Tupán, camisán, iopnán, soihé, ejé, ajatocó). The authors explicitly flag this as speculation; the language is extinct and known only from two short 19th-c. naturalists' wordlists, so no first-hand prosodic description can ever exist.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the authors note only that 'most' (not all) diacritics in the records are on the final vowel. Primary collectors' own remarks concern gutturals/nasals and vowel length ('kurz', 'L'i est long'), not accent.
new_statements.domain_note: 'última sílaba da palavra (fonológica?)' -- word domain, with the authors themselves querying whether the phonological word is the right unit; evidence is isolated citation forms in wordlists.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Malalí [mala1432] itself, as recorded by Wied-Neuwied (1815-17) and Saint-Hilaire (c. 1817) at the Santo Antônio/Porto de Santa Cruz settlements near Peçanha (Suaçuí Grande, Rio Doce basin), Minas Gerais. The statement is an inference by the modern analysts, not an observation by the collectors; the comparanda named (Maxakalí maxa1247, Pataxó-Hãhãhãe pata1261, Krenák kren1239, Ritual Maxakalí ~ capo1236/macu1258) are sister languages, not Malalí varieties.

new_statements.rule_in_words: For 'Maxakali Ritual' (the Language of the Ritual Songs, which Nikulin 2020:18 and Nikulin & Silva 2020:7 equate with the 19th-c. Makuni complex incl. Martius's 'Macuni' = macu1258), the authors state from their own recordings/transcriptions that stress is non-contrastive and word-final. For Macuni as recorded in 1816-1818 (Wied, Saint-Hilaire, Eschwege) no author states a rule; Saint-Hilaire (1830 II:214 n.1) explicitly says he did not attend to accentuation, though the accents he did write on Macuni forms (II:48) are nearly all final (Tupá, tatán, atinán, etcoló, nhimcotó, canhá).
new_statements.domain_note: word (phonological word); statement made in passing in a paper on the sister language Malali, asserted for Maxakali Ritual as performed today by Maxakali speakers (Campos 2009:30-31 transcriptions of ritual-language words likewise all show final stress).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog macu1258 'Macuni' is the language of three 1816-1818 wordlists (Wied-Neuwied 1821 II:323-325 'Maconis'; Saint-Hilaire 1830 II:47-48 'Macunis', Alto dos Bois near Minas Novas; Eschwege), compiled by Martius 1867 II:173-176. Nikulin (2020:18) tags 'Maxakali Ritual [capo1236, macu1258]' and groups Macuni with Machacari/Capoxo/Cumanacho/Panhame as the 'Makuni' dialect complex, 'muito proximo ao Maxakali Ritual' (the Lingua dos Cantos Rituais still sung by Maxakali [maxa1247] speakers). The quoted stress statement is about Maxakali Ritual as recorded from modern Maxakali performers, not about the 19th-c. Macuni records themselves, for which no stress statement exists (Saint-Hilaire disclaims accent notation). Modern spoken Maxakali (maxa1247, already catalogued separately) also has final stress.

sources.note: sec. 2 Fonologia, p. 8: no dedicated prosody section; authors 'speculate' that stress was non-contrastive and fell on the last syllable of the (phonological?) word, by analogy with Maxakalí, Ritual Maxakalí, Pataxó-Hãhãhãe and Krenák, and because most diacritic accents in the 19th-c. Malalí records sit on the word-final vowel. Appendix A (pp. 49-56) reproduces the Wied-Neuwied, Saint-Hilaire and Martius lists in full (e.g. ‹camisán›SH, ‹tupán›SH, ‹iopnán›SH, ‹soihé›W, ‹ejé›W, ‹ajatocó›W).
